tweets.text:
While we're all waiting for Fable 5.5, GPT-6.1 Astra, and Bel, something much bigger is happening behind the scenes, and I don't think we're paying nearly enough attention. Let me explain...

Companies like Nvidia and major cloud providers are investing billions into AI labs. Those labs then turn around and spend that money buying chips and computing power from the very same companies funding them.

Think about that for a second.

You invest billions into a company, that company spends those billions buying your products, your revenue goes up, investors get excited, and the cycle continues.

Everyone looks like they're winning.

But here's the problem: how much of this growth comes from actual customers, and how much depends on companies continuously financing each other?

What happens when that money slows down?

And the craziest part is that we're so obsessed with getting smarter models, better benchmarks, and higher usage limits that we barely stop to question any of this.

I'm guilty of that too. I LOVE AI, and I genuinely believe it's going to change humanity forever.

But that's exactly why this worries me.

The technology can be revolutionary while the financial system supporting it becomes dangerously unstable.

We need to stop treating every new breakthrough as proof that everything happening behind the scenes is fine.

The AI revolution can succeed while the AI financial bubble bursts.

And I think a lot of people are forgetting that.
